rendered:
Retention after cycling at 0.5C[1]: the best LLTO coating was LLTO-2, the 2 mol.%[2] coating, at 86.2%[3]. For comparison, LLTO-0.5 retained 85.5%[4] and LLTO-1 retained 57.2%[5]. The paper gives these as capacity retention, not absolute capacities. The pristine NCM, by contrast, only retained 56.6% of its initial discharge capacity after 200 cycles[6]. So the LLTO-2 coated NCM kept clearly more of its capacity than the pristine NCM, and LLTO-0.5 performed about as well as LLTO-2.

Rate capability: the LLTO coating in general improved it, as the paper states: LLTO coated NCM materials exhibited improved rate capability[7]. The paper attributes this to the high ionic conductivity of the LLTO layer and to suppression of side reactions between electrolyte and cathode. For the 2 mol.%[8] coating, the paper reports a drop in rate capability and suggests the cause: However, with 2 mol.% coating, the rate capability decreased, which may be due to the increase in the thickness of the coating layer, resulting in the suppression of electron transfer process during charge/discharge cycling[9]. In short, the authors suggest the thicker 2 mol.%[10] layer hindered electron transfer during charge and discharge. They offer this as a possible explanation ("may be due to"). The rate data itself is only shown in the figure, not given as numbers in the text.
